findings.text: CheckDrafts accepts a `defer` reply that omits `body`, but `skills/verdict/schemas/drain-replies.schema.json` requires `body` on every reply (required: thread_id, waiting_comment_id, disposition, body) and the handed spec says body is required. `validate.sh` rejects the artifact with `missing required key(s): body` while verdict accepts it, so a draft can pass validation and still be schema-invalid.

The envelope's `next` says to run `--post` whenever `--agent` was passed, even when zero pending threads mean no agent launched and no drafts were written (and the same happens when every pending thread is skipped `no-draft`). The handed spec says `next` names the command the run did not do; here it points at a step with no drafts and, in this build, an unrecognised flag.
findings.quote: return "post the drafts with verdict drain " + req.Repo + " " + req.Pr + " --post"

findings.text: Direct selection of the embedded `*Runtime` field panics when an in-process caller supplies a `Request` without a Runtime; `refreshRequest` immediately below explicitly guards that same nil case, so the two halves of the verb disagree. A reproduced call to `selfLogin` with `Request{Repo:..., Pr:...}` panics instead of returning `drain-failed`.

`--max-threads` is validated only after `RunThreads` has rewritten `threads.json`, as are the truncated-feed, login and ledger refusals in `readInputs`; the handed spec requires `drain-failed` for a truncated feed before any write and says every refusal comes before the first write. A bad cap or unreadable login therefore leaves a mutated bundle on a failed invocation.
